Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:12:1.hebrew: במגירה - שיג"א, סכין שיש בה פגימות הרבה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:12:1.english: With a saw - *Scie* [Old French for saw], a knife that has many notches.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:13:1.english: Benefit from its value - If he rented it out to others.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:14:1.english: [Deriving] benefit from its body - Such as shearing and labor.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:18:1.hebrew: מה פדייה מותרת - דלאחר פדיונו, דברי הכל שרי בהנאה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:18:1.english: Just as redemption permits - For after its redemption, all agree that it is permitted to derive benefit [from it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:19:1.english: He caused a loss of the money of a priest - In that he did not redeem it with a lamb and give it to a priest.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:19:2.hebrew: לפיכך יופסד ממונו - יכפוהו בית דין לעורפו לאחר שלשים, כדמפרש בפירקא, ויאסר בהנאה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:19:2.english: Therefore, his money shall be lost - The court compels him to break its neck after thirty [days], as is explained in the chapter, and it will be forbidden to derive benefit [from it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:1:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן כגון ששחטו - לפטר חמור. ואי דשחטיה לשם שחיטה גמורה, אפי' לר' שמעון הויא מחשבה ומטמא; אלא בשחטו ע"מ להתלמד בו הלכות שחיטה. ובהך פליגי: דרבנן סברי הך שחיטה משויא לה אוכל כשחיטה גמורה מעלייתא, דאמרינן בהעור והרוטב (חולין קיז:) "השוחט בהמה לעובד כוכבים כו'", כדפרישית לעיל; ור"ש סבר הך שחיטה לאו מעלייתא היא, ולא הויא מחשבה. ובפלוגתא דנימוס ור"א:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:1:1.english: Here, we are dealing with [a case] where he slaughtered [it] - [This refers to] a firstborn donkey. And if [the case were] that he slaughtered it for the sake of a full slaughter, even according to Rabbi Shimon [this act] would constitute intent [for food] and it would become susceptible to impurity; rather, [the case is] where he slaughtered it in order to teach himself the laws of slaughter. And regarding this they disagree: for the Rabbis maintain that this slaughter renders it [susceptible to impurity as] food, just like a proper, full slaughter — as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaOred VeHaRotev (Chullin 117b): “One who slaughters an animal for a gentile, etc.,” as I explained above; and Rabbi Shimon maintains that this slaughter is not a proper one, and does not constitute intent. And [their dispute is] in accordance with the dispute between Nimos and Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:20:1.hebrew: הא מיפסד וקאי - דמחיים נמי אסור, ומאי מפסדא ליה עריפה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:20:1.english: It is already lost - For while alive it is also forbidden, and what loss does breaking [its] neck cause him?

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:20:2.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Shimon - And after breaking [its] neck, he concedes [that deriving benefit is prohibited].

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:22:1.hebrew: דביני וביני - דמחיים נמי אסור בהנאה, מצי פריק ליה בשה בר דנקא, והשתא מפסיד הכל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:22:1.english: [The difference] between [them] - For [even though] while alive it is also forbidden to derive benefit [from it], he could have redeemed it with a lamb worth a _danka_ [one-sixth of a dinar], and now he loses everything.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:23:1.hebrew: איבעית אימא ר' שמעון - ואפילו הכי, בהנאה לא מיתסר. ומאי אפסיד ממונו? לפחת מיתה — מה שמיתה פיחתתו, דמחיים הוה שוה מנה, ולאחר מיתה אינה שוה אלא דינר, להאכילו לכלבו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:23:1.english: If you wish, say [it is] Rabbi Shimon - And even so, it is not forbidden for benefit. And what [is the meaning of] “he caused a loss to his money”? [It refers] to the depreciation of death — that which death depreciated its [value], for while alive it was worth a maneh, and after death it is worth only a dinar, to feed it to his dog.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:25:1.hebrew: להא דרב נחמן - דאמר לעיל: מודה ר' שמעון לאחר עריפה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:25:1.english: This [statement] of Rav Naḥman - Who said above: Rabbi Shimon concedes after the breaking of the neck.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:26:1.english: She should be betrothed with all of it - For all of it is permitted for benefit.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:27:1.hebrew: שאינו שוה אלא שקל - סלע, דהשתא ליכא ביני ביני, דההוא שה דיהבינן לכהן תותיה בעי למיהוי שוה שקל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:27:1.english: Where it is worth only a shekel - [That is,] a sela, so that now there is no difference between them, as that lamb which we give to the priest in its stead must be worth a shekel.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:27:2.english: “You shall redeem,” “you shall redeem” - It is written twice: “And a firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 13:13).

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:29:1.english: [It] is juxtaposed with the firstborn of man - As it is written: “The firstborn of man and the firstborn of an unclean animal you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:15).

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:29:2.hebrew: מה בכור אדם - פדיונו לאחר שלשים יום — "ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה" — וחמשה סלעים בעי למיתב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:29:2.english: Just as a firstborn of man - His redemption is after thirty days — "and their redemption-money, from a month old you shall redeem" — and one is required to give five sela.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:29:3.english: Here too, after thirty days and five - One must give [five] sela’im.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:2:1.hebrew: דמו מכשיר - אם נפל על הזרעים. וכל שכן אם שחטו שחיטה גמורה, דמו מכשיר אפילו לגופיה, דשחיטתו הויא מחשבתו. ואי נחרו ולא שחטו, תו לא הוה פליג בה רבי אלעזר, דודאי לעלמא הוא דמכשיר דמו ולאו לגופיה, דאיהו גופיה לא מקבל טומאה בלא מחשבה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:2:1.english: Its blood renders susceptible - If it fell upon seeds. And all the more so, if he slaughtered it with a full slaughter, its blood renders susceptible even [the bird] itself, as its slaughter constitutes its designation [as food]. And if he stabbed it and did not slaughter it, Rabbi Elazar would no longer have disagreed about it, for its blood certainly renders other [foods] susceptible and not [the bird] itself, as it itself does not contract impurity without designation.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:3:1.hebrew: אלא לאו איסורו חישובו - הוא דאיכא בהדי שחיטה, כה"ג איכא בינייהו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:3:1.english: Rather, is it not [that] its prohibition [serves as] its intent - It is [that] which is present alongside slaughter — in such a case [is the dispute] between them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:4:1.hebrew: לעלמא - אם נפל על הזרעים. אבל לגופיה בעי מחשבה, דאיסורו חישובו גרידא לא אמרינן, והך שחיטה לא חשיבא לשווייה אוכל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:4:1.english: In general - If it fell upon seeds. But for [the crow] itself, intent is required, for we do not say that its prohibition alone constitutes its intent, and this slaughter is not significant [enough] to render it a food.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:6:1.hebrew: הואיל ויש בו סימני טהרה - כדאמר באלו טריפות (חולין סא:), משום הכי הוי אוכלא. אבל לגבי פטר חמור דלית ליה סימני טהרה, אי לאו דחשיב — משום הך שחיטה לא מטמו ליה רבנן; ור' שמעון, אע"ג דחשיב עליה, פליג — משום דאסור בהנאה לאחר עריפה, כדרב':
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:6:1.english: Since it has indicators of purity - As [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] “Elu Tereifot” (Chullin 61b), because of this it is considered food. But regarding a firstborn donkey, which has no indicators of purity: if he had not designated it [for consumption], the Rabbis would not deem it susceptible to impurity on account of this slaughter; and Rabbi Shimon, even though he designated it [for consumption], disagrees — because deriving benefit [from it] is forbidden after the breaking of its neck, in accordance with [the statement of] Rabba.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:7:1.hebrew: ומנלן דסימני טהרה מילתא - לאחותי לידי טומאה, דקתני עלה בברייתא דלעיל: נבלת בהמה טהורה כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:7:1.english: And from where do we [derive] that indicators of a kosher [animal] are a [significant] matter - To bring [it] into [susceptibility to] impurity; as it was taught regarding it in the baraita [cited] above: "The carcass of a kosher animal, etc."

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:8:1.hebrew: אפי' להתעסק - דמתכוין לחתוך דבר אחר, דלאו לשחיטה איכוין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:8:1.english: Even acting unawares - Where one intends to cut something else, so that he did not intend for slaughter.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:8:2.hebrew: אין הכי נמי ומשום נימוס - להודיע כחו, דאע"ג דשחטו להתלמד בו — דהוי שחיטה חשובה טפי מלהתעסק — אפ"ה איהו גופיה לא מטמא ליה נימוס:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:8:2.english: Yes, this is indeed so, and because of Nimos - To make known his strength [in being lenient], that even though he slaughtered it to teach himself with it — which is a more significant [act of] slaughter than [merely] acting unawares — even so, Nimos himself does not deem it susceptible to impurity.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:9:1.hebrew: איתיביה - אביי לרבא, דאמר: מודה רבי שמעון לאחר עריפה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:9:1.english: He raised an objection to him - Abaye [raised an objection] to Rava, who said: Rabbi Shimon concedes after the breaking of the neck.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:9:2.hebrew: בקופיץ - סכין גדול, שכן דרך עריפה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:9:2.english: With a cleaver - A large knife, for such is the manner of breaking the neck.

Rashi on Bekhorot 10b:9:3.english: From behind - Opposite the nape of its neck, as it is written: “And you shall break its neck” [va’arafto].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 10b:2:1.hebrew: שהשוחט עורב להתלמד דמו מכשיר - פירש הקונט': "אם נפל על הזרעים; וכ"ש אם שחטו שחיטה גמורה — דמו מכשיר אפילו לגופיה, דשחיטתו מחשבתו. ואם נחרו ולא שחטו — תו לא פליג ר' אליעזר, דודאי לעלמא מכשיר דמו, ולא לגופיה, דאיהו גופיה לא מקבל טומאה בלא מחשבה", עכל"ה. ותימה: פירש דדם נחירה מכשיר לעלמא — דמה טעם יכשיר, כיון דלא הוי דם שחיטה, ודם חללים לא שייך בבהמה אלא באדם:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 10b:2:1.english: "That one who slaughters a crow to teach himself, its blood renders [food] susceptible" - Rashi explained: If [its blood] fell upon seeds [it renders them susceptible to impurity]; and all the more so if he slaughtered it with a full slaughter, its blood renders susceptible even with regard to [the crow] itself, for its slaughter constitutes its intent [to treat it as food]. And if he stabbed it and did not slaughter it, Rabbi Eliezer would no longer disagree, for its blood certainly renders [other foods] in general susceptible, but not [the crow] itself, since it itself does not contract impurity without intent. Thus far are his words. And it is astonishing that he explained that the blood of stabbing renders [other foods] in general susceptible — for what reason would it render [them] susceptible, since it is not the blood of slaughter, and [the rule of] the blood of the slain does not apply to an animal, but only to a human!

Tosafot on Bekhorot 10b:6:1.hebrew: שאני עורב הואיל ויש בו סימני טהרה - הוא הדין כ"ד עופות חוץ מנשר, כדמוכח פרק אלו טרפות (חולין סא:):
Tosafot on Bekhorot 10b:6:1.english: "A crow is different, since it has indicators of purity" - The same applies to the twenty-four [species of non-kosher] birds except for the eagle [nesher], as is demonstrated in the chapter [entitled] Elu Tereifot (Chullin 61b).

Tosafot on Bekhorot 10b:8:1.hebrew: מאי איריא להתלמד אפי' להתעסק - פירוש: ואפי' נחרו נמי, דלהתעסק נמי לאו שחיטה היא, וכנחרו דמי. ואע"ג דאז לא היה הוכשר בדם שחיטה, מ"מ פריך: כיון דלא אתי לאשמועינן דדם שחיטה מכשיר — דהא כבר אשמועינן — ולא בא לאשמועינן אלא דאין צריך מחשבה, הואיל ויש בו סימני טהרה, זה היה יכול לאשמועינן בלא שחיטה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 10b:8:1.english: "Why specifically to teach oneself? Even [if he] acted unawares" - Explanation: And [the Gemara means] even if he stabbed it as well, for [acting] unawares is also not a [valid] slaughter, and is considered like [one who] stabbed it. And even though then it would not have been rendered susceptible [to impurity] by the blood of slaughter, nevertheless [the Gemara] asks: Since it does not come to teach us that the blood of slaughter renders [food] susceptible — for it already taught us this — and it came to teach us only that it does not require intention [to be food], since it has kosher indicators, this could have been taught without slaughter [at all].
